newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Stock Exchange votes to demutualise.
newsitem.headline: Australia Stock Exchange votes to demutualise.

text.p: In an historic vote on Friday, members of the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) approved a plan to clear the way for the ASX to be the first publicly listed stock exchange in the world.

At special meetings held simultaneously in all of Australia's capital cities, members approved the proposal which will allow the ASX to dismantle its mutual structure and seek Federal legislation to allow it to become a public company.

Speaking after the meeting ASX chairman Maurice Newman said keen interest had been shown in the move from the Paris and Toronto stock exchanges who had asked to be promptly informed about the results of the meeting.
The vote was a significant step in the move towards demutualisation, Newman said, but much work needed to be done to resolve a range of regulatory and supervision issues that arose from the decision.
"We have already commenced discussions with the Federal government and the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) on these matters and are grateful for their cooperation," he said.
Under the demutualisation, the ASX plans to draft new articles of association while the membership rules will be overhauled to allow for a broader membership base that reflects other exchange users.
Newman said the ASX board's best guess at how long the whole process would take to complete was 12 to 15 months. "It's our best guess, but many issues could arise," he said.

Newman added it was ASX's intention to establish the deepest and most liquid market possible for ASX shares. "Anyone will be able to own a share. We feel that listing is the best way of promoting broad ownership," he said.
The ASX could be listed with independent supervision arrangements to be worked out with the ASC, Newman said.
It is unclear what value would be attached to the shares included in the demutualisation, as they would only be issued after the Federal Government sanctioned the process.
If the ASX had listed on June 30, 1996 the approximate value would have been A$242,000 (US$191,000) per member, he said.
The ASX currently has 522 individual members and 88 corporate members.
It reported a surplus after tax and abnormal items of A$19.39 million (US$15.32 million) in the year to June 30, 1996, up from A$14.65 million in 1994/95.
